title: The Princes Who Vanished in the Tower
hook: In 1483, two young princes entered the Tower of London, a fortress in England’s capital, and vanished.
full_narration: In 1483, two young princes entered the Tower of London, a fortress in England’s capital, and vanished. Their father, King Edward the Fourth, died, leaving twelve-year-old Edward as heir. [[pause:0.4]] Edward was brought to the Tower, which was then used as a royal palace. His younger brother, Richard of York, joined him, both waiting for coronation. [[voice:tense]] Their uncle, Richard of Gloucester, the royal guardian, controlled access and the kingdom’s soldiers. Then Richard declared the boys illegitimate, meaning not legal heirs, and took the crown. [[pause:0.6]] If the princes lived, rivals could rally England against Richard’s throne. By late summer 1483, public sightings stopped, and whispers moved through London. In 1485, Henry Tudor defeated Richard, but the princes never returned. [[voice:low]] No proof named their killer; the Tower still keeps their fate. [[pause:0.8]] Follow for more dark history.

youtube_description: In 1483, two royal brothers entered the Tower of London and disappeared from public view. Edward, the young heir to England’s throne, and his brother Richard of York were placed under the control of their uncle, Richard of Gloucester. Soon after, Richard declared them illegitimate and became king himself. Their disappearance threatened his rule, fed rebellion, and left England with a mystery that still has no proven answer. This short cinematic history script follows the fear, power, and silence surrounding the Princes in the Tower.
